claims.title: Exact finite rational simplex-grid drift game
claims.scope: finite categorical source laws restricted to a declared rational denominator grid with exact total-variation transitions and finite deterministic codebooks
assumptions: the initial source law lies exactly on the declared grid
all law pairs, source paths, codebooks, and code sequences complete below configured caps
source-law transitions are adversarial within the declared finite graph
nonclaims: the finite grid is not silently identified with the continuous simplex
complete finite enumeration is not a polynomial-time scalability result

claims.title: Drift information-pattern value hierarchy
claims.scope: the declared finite-grid open-loop, delayed-feedback, current-law-feedback, and clairvoyant deterministic coding games
assumptions: the source adversary and designer both know the game and information pattern
the designer minimizes and nature maximizes the same cumulative source and switching cost
the codebook universe is identical across the four games
nonclaims: the hierarchy orders values under nested designer information sets rather than asserting one information pattern describes reality

claims.title: Zero switching cost equates current-law feedback and clairvoyance
claims.scope: finite-horizon deterministic coding when the designer observes each current source law before acting and codebook changes have zero cost
assumptions: period source cost is q_t dot ell_c
there is no interperiod codebook constraint or switching penalty
the same deterministic code universe is available in every period
nonclaims: positive switching costs can make clairvoyance strictly more valuable
the equality does not cover hidden or noisily estimated current laws

claims.title: Finite-grid open-loop adversary is a restriction of the continuous path adversary
claims.scope: one common initial law, TV transition budget, identical deterministic code-sequence universe, and a grid contained in the continuous simplex
assumptions: every grid transition is feasible in the continuous source-law model
the objective and switching penalties agree between models
nonclaims: grid and continuous values need not be equal
the grid value is a lower bound on adversarial cost rather than a conservative upper bound

claims.title: Uniform K3 has a strict four-level information value separation
claims.scope: complete three-state confusion graph, uniform initial law, denominator six, eta=1/6, horizon two, and switching cost 1/4
assumptions: the exact source law is observed in the feedback games
the whole future path is known only in the clairvoyant benchmark
nonclaims: the exact fractions are specific to the declared finite instance
the result does not price the mechanism used to observe a source law

claims.title: Bounded exact drift Bellman and path audit
claims.scope: the rational simplex grids, transition graphs, code sequences, Bellman tables, and witness paths exercised by the repository tests
assumptions: all configured law-pair, path, code, and sequence caps complete without truncation
Python Fraction arithmetic is used for finite costs and transitions
nonclaims: CI success is not a continuum or scalability theorem
finite coding-game checks are not evidence that reality is simulated
